readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckTensorSecondJet.tensorHessian_hasFDerivAt
readback.mathematical_statement:
Let E = EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), with its Euclidean norm, Bilin = E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1 = E ->L[R] Bilin, and Jet2 = E ->L[R] Jet1. Bilin and both derivative-jet spaces use the iterated continuous-linear-map operator norms; the four displayed local instances explicitly choose the canonical normed additive groups and real normed spaces on Jet1 and Jet2. For every real alpha and T, every W : (Fin 3 x Fin 3) -> ParabolicSolutionGraph.Graph alpha T, every real t, and every z : E, if 0 <= t <= T then the map y |-> tensorJet W (t,y), with values in the full Jet1 space, has ordinary real Frechet derivative tensorHessian W (t,z) at z. This is HasFDerivAt on all of E, not a within-set derivative and not merely an equality after evaluation in selected directions.

Write T_ab = the fixed Bilin-valued DeTurckTensorBasis.tensor a b, and write u_ab, du_ab, ddu_ab for the corresponding fields of W(a,b). The pinned definitions give tensorValue W q = sum_(a,b in Fin 3) u_ab(q) * T_ab; tensorJet W q applied to a direction r is sum_(a,b) du_ab(q)(r) * T_ab; and tensorHessian W q applied in the ordered slots r,s,v,w is sum_(a,b) ddu_ab(q)(r)(s) * T_ab(v)(w). The first slot r differentiates the Jet1-valued map, s is the existing spatial derivative slot, and v,w are the two tensor slots. All nine ordered entry pairs are retained. No symmetry of W, no restriction to symmetric Bilin values, no directional-slot contraction, and no symmetrization is assumed or concluded by this declaration.

Each Graph contains u and ut with real values, du with values E ->L[R] R, and ddu with values E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R. All four are members of the unchanged Y alpha T carrier: globally bounded functions on R x E, zero outside the cylinder [0,T] x E, with bounded scaled parabolic differences on that cylinder. The parabolic distance is norm(x-y) + sqrt(abs(t-s)); the Y norm is its supremum norm plus the supremum of norm(f(p)-f(q))/parabolicDist(p,q)^alpha over distinct ordered cylinder pairs, with zero inserted for the empty case. The Graph norm is norm(u)+norm(ut)+norm(du)+norm(ddu). The finite nine-entry function space has its existing Pi norm, the maximum of these Graph norms, not their sum. Graph certificates require u(0,x)=0 for every x, HasFDerivAt of x |-> u(t,x) with derivative du(t,x), HasFDerivAt of x |-> du(t,x) with derivative ddu(t,x), and HasDerivWithinAt of s |-> u(s,x) with derivative ut(t,x) within [0,T], at every t in [0,T] and every x. In this conclusion only the genuine spatial derivative certificates are used to identify the displayed Hessian. There is no explicit norm estimate or quantitative constant in the theorem.

There is no assumption alpha > 0, alpha < 1, or T > 0. The implication is empty when [0,T] is empty; it includes t=0 and t=T whenever the interval is nonempty. No spatial cutoff, compact support, chart, metric invertibility, or positivity is part of this statement. Time-cylinder zero extension is inherited from Graph; it supplies no spatial compact-support claim.

readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckTensorSecondJet.tensorValue_contDiff_two
readback.mathematical_statement:
Use the same E, full Bilin, canonical iterated operator-norm Jet1 and Jet2 spaces, nine-entry Pi-norm Inputs alpha T, and unchanged Graph/Y carriers just described. For every real alpha and T, every W : Inputs alpha T, and every real t, if 0 < alpha and 0 <= t <= T, the map y : E |-> tensorValue W (t,y) is ContDiff R (2 : WithTop ENat) on all of E. Thus each fixed-time Bilin-valued slice is twice continuously Frechet differentiable, with both tensor slots retained and with the full first and ordered second spatial derivative carriers supplied by the genuine scalar Graph entries. Its pinned value definition is the complete sum over all nine ordered (a,b) entries u_ab(t,y) * DeTurckTensorBasis.tensor a b.

The positivity requirement applies only to alpha in this declaration; there is no alpha < 1, T > 0, symmetry, metric, cutoff, or additional regularity premise. The t hypothesis includes either endpoint of a nonempty interval. This asserts global spatial C2 for a fixed t, not joint space-time C2, not an ordinary time derivative at an endpoint, and not C-infinity. No norm inequality, spatial compact-support conclusion, identification with a metric variation, or local equality with a separate field is included.
